counterfactual_missing_items: No family history of neurofibromatosis (contradicts neurofibroma)
Imaging features more consistent with schwannoma than glomus tumor
Lesions follow nerve course without invasion (supports nerve sheath tumor)
decisive_items: On T2-weighted fat-suppressed images, they were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration; each was surrounded by a hyperintense rim.
A small extension of high signal from the lateral aspect of one lesion resembled a “mouse-tail.”
response.rationale: R2 directly states the suspected diagnosis and provides multiple raw imaging features (T1 isointense, T2 hyperintense, mouse-tail sign) that are characteristic of plexiform schwannoma. C1 adds anatomical specificity (common plantar digital nerves) but relies on a single raw span and is an append-only completion of R2; R2 is more comprehensive and directly matches the vignette's final impression. R3 is contradicted by absent neurofibromatosis history, and R1 lacks imaging support despite symptom overlap.

rejected.why: Contradicted by no family history of neurofibromatosis; imaging pattern more suggestive of schwannoma.
Symptoms (cold/compression pain) are suggestive but imaging findings (T1/T2 signal, mouse-tail) are not typical of glomus tumor; differential diagnosis includes it but is not favored.
